_: What `just acknowledgements` (internal/acknowledgements/gen) can't find in a lock file, and how it
names what it does find. It finds by itself: the Go modules linked into hmk, hmkd and pane-holder (for
macOS and Linux) and libhmkquic (for Android), the Swift packages in apple/Package.resolved, the npm packages bundled into
apple/Resources/editor.html, the Maven artifacts in the Android app's release build (from Gradle), and the
rows of THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Each Maven artifact goes in the component whose "maven" (group:artifact
prefixes) matches it, and must match one; "aarNotices" adds the notices Google's AARs carry for what they
bundle, from the artifacts its prefixes match. The licence texts come from those packages' own files, never typed here: "{maven:group:artifact}!path"
is a file inside that artifact. {ghostty_src}, {cef_dir}, {goroot} and {repo} are filled in by it;
{ghostty}, {cef} and {go} are their versions. A missing file stops it: fix the path here (a new Ghostty
commit can move its dependencies' folders in {ghostty_src}/zig-pkg).
